draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Cherthala! The pooram at the Karthyayani Devi Temple here is called the second most famous pooram in Kerala. Head west and you hit a string of beaches, some of which are never crowded.
draft.hungryLine: Cherthala is seafood country, think fish roast and fish curries, washed down with tender coconut picked right in front of you.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Velorvattom Sri Mahadeva Temple is a 7 minute walk and Kuttikattu Sree Bhadra Kali Devi Temple is about 9, both easy starts.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Go to Andhakaranazhy Beach, about 10 km from town, for the sunset.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Velorvattom Sri Mahadeva Temple is one of the few temples in Kerala with two Nalambalams and two flagmasts.

seeFirst.caption: Short walks and a short drive

spots.name: Velorvattom Sri Mahadeva Temple
spots.detail: 7 min walk · One of the 108 Shiva temples, with two flagmasts

spots.name: Kuttikattu Sree Bhadra Kali Devi Temple
spots.detail: 9 min walk · A local Bhadrakali temple

spots.name: Karthyayani Devi Temple, Cherthala
spots.detail: Short drive · Home of the famous Cherthala pooram

legends.title: Parasurama's Shiva
legends.body: Legend says Kerala is the land gifted by Lord Parasurama. The sage is said to have installed the Shiva idol here himself.

legends.title: The miraculous statue
legends.body: The church's statue of the Passion of Our Lord is held to be miraculous. Thousands come every year on a pilgrimage of repentance and new beginnings.

tips.title: Save the evening for the beach.
tips.body: Andhakaranazhy Beach, about 10 km away, is the best sunset spot around town.

tips.title: Mind temple etiquette.
tips.body: Cherthala's temples are lovely places to sit, but take care not to break any customs or rules.

story.title: An ancient Shiva temple
story.body: Velorvattom Sri Mahadeva Temple is believed to have been built by Azhvanchery Thamprakkal. Its exact date of installation isn't known.

story.title: A shrine by the sea
story.body: The Portuguese built the shrine at Arthunkal, and it is still kept intact. Today it's one of six basilicas in Kerala, with Arthunkal beach right in front.

story.title: Pooram and pilgrims
story.body: Cherthala pooram draws huge crowds to the Karthyayani Devi Temple. Thousands also head to Thankey Church on pilgrimage.

story.title: Beaches and backwaters
story.body: Cherthala sits on National Highway 66, about 22 km north of Alappuzha. Beaches lie to the west and backwaters and Thanneermukkom to the east.
